Defaults to \u003ccode\u003etable\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAliases\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eapps\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003einvoke\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-invoke\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: invoke\" href=\"#invoke\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eInvoke an authentication method, a trigger, or a create/search action locally or remotely.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier invoke [ACTIONTYPE] [ACTIONKEY]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis command allows you to invoke your integration's authentication, triggers, and actions. With this tool, you can test and debug your integration code directly from your terminal without leaving your development environment and opening a browser.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhy use this command?\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFast feedback loops: Verify your code changes instantly.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eStep-by-step debugging: Use a debugger to step through your code locally.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUntruncated logs: View complete HTTP logs and errors in your terminal.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eModes\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-modes\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Modes\" href=\"#modes\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003einvoke\u003c/code\u003e command works in three modes:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLocal mode (default): runs your code locally, and sends outgoing requests directly from your local machine.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRelay mode (experimental): runs your code locally, but proxies all outgoing requests through Zapier using production authentication data.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eRemote mode: runs your code and sends outgoing requests entirely in/from Zapier production environment.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eLocal mode\u003c/strong\u003e is the default mode. Without the \u003ccode\u003e--remote\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e-r\u003c/code\u003e) flag or the \u003ccode\u003e--authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e) flag, the command runs in local mode. It's useful when you want to quickly test your integration code locally. You'll need to set up local auth data in the \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file using the \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth start\u003c/code\u003e command.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRelay mode\u003c/strong\u003e is currently experimental. It's enabled when the \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e flag is specified. It's useful when you want to test code locally but setting up local auth data is troublesome, such as when your OAuth2 server requires a non-localhost or HTTPS redirect URI. By specifying \u003ccode\u003e-a \u0026lt;authentication-id\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e, all outgoing requests will be proxied through Zapier's relay service using the production auth data with the given authentication ID. See the \u003cstrong\u003eAuthentication\u003c/strong\u003e section below for more details.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBoth local and relay mode \u003cstrong\u003eemulate\u003c/strong\u003e how your code would run in Zapier production environment, so the behavior might not be exactly the same. But we consider every inconsistency a bug or a limitation to be fixed. For 100% match with production behavior, use remote mode.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eRemote mode\u003c/strong\u003e is enabled when the \u003ccode\u003e--remote\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e-r\u003c/code\u003e) flag is specified. It's useful when you want to verify how your code behaves in Zapier production environment. Note that remote mode requires deploying your integration first. If the \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e flag is not specified, the command will prompt you to select one of your available authentications/connections in production. By default, the remote mode invokes the \u003ccode\u003eversion\u003c/code\u003e set in your \u003ccode\u003epackage.json\u003c/code\u003e. You can use the \u003ccode\u003e--version\u003c/code\u003e (or \u003ccode\u003e-v\u003c/code\u003e) flag to specify a different deployed version.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eAuthentication\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-authentication\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Authentication\" href=\"#authentication\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can supply the authentcation data in two ways: Load from the local \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file or use the \u003ccode\u003e--authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e flag.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe local \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the-local-env-file\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The local .env file\" href=\"#the-local-env-file\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis command loads environment variables and \u003ccode\u003eauthData\u003c/code\u003e from the \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file in the current directory. If you don't have a \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file yet, you can use the \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth start\u003c/code\u003e command to help you initialize it, or you can manually create it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth start\u003c/code\u003e subcommand will prompt you for the necessary auth fields and save them to the \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file. For OAuth2, it will start a local HTTP server, open the authorization URL in the browser, wait for the OAuth2 redirect, and get the access token.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEach line in the \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file should follow one of these formats:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eVAR_NAME=VALUE\u003c/code\u003e for environment variables\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eauthData_FIELD_KEY=VALUE\u003c/code\u003e for auth data fields\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eFor example, a \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file for an OAuth2 integration might look like this:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"CLIENT_ID='your_client_id'\nCLIENT_SECRET='your_client_secret'\nauthData_access_token='1234567890'\nauthData_refresh_token='abcdefg'\nauthData_account_name='zapier'\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eCLIENT_ID='your_client_id'\nCLIENT_SECRET='your_client_secret'\nauthData_access_token='1234567890'\nauthData_refresh_token='abcdefg'\nauthData_account_name='zapier'\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e flag\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-the---authentication-id-flag\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: The --authentication-id flag\" href=\"#the---authentication-id-flag\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSetting up local auth data can be troublesome. For instance, in OAuth2, you may have to configure your app server to allow localhost redirect URIs or use a port forwarding tool. This is sometimes not easy to get right.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e flag (\u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e for short) gives you an alternative (and perhaps easier) way to supply your auth data. You can use \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e to specify an existing production authentication/connection. The available authentications can be found at \u003ca href=\"https://zapier.com/app/assets/connections\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://zapier.com/app/assets/connections\u003c/a\u003e. Check \u003ca href=\"https://zpr.io/z8SjFTdnTFZ2\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://zpr.io/z8SjFTdnTFZ2\u003c/a\u003e for more instructions.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen \u003ccode\u003e-a -\u003c/code\u003e is specified, such as \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth test -a -\u003c/code\u003e, the command will interactively prompt you to select one of your available authentications.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf you know your authentication ID, you can specify it directly, such as \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth test -a 123456\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e flag also works in remote mode with the \u003ccode\u003e-r\u003c/code\u003e flag. In remote mode, if \u003ccode\u003e-a\u003c/code\u003e is not specified, such as \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke -r\u003c/code\u003e, the command will prompt you to select one of your available authentications.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eTesting authentication\u003c/h4\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-testing-authentication\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Testing authentication\" href=\"#testing-authentication\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo test if the auth data is correct, run either one of these:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"zapier-platform invoke auth test   # invokes authentication.test method\nzapier-platform invoke auth label  # invokes authentication.test and renders connection label\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth test   # invokes authentication.test method\nzapier-platform invoke auth label  # invokes authentication.test and renders connection label\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo refresh stale auth data for OAuth2 or session auth, run \u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth refresh\u003c/code\u003e. Note that refreshing is only applicable for local auth data in the \u003ccode\u003e.env\u003c/code\u003e file.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eInvoking a trigger or an action\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-invoking-a-trigger-or-an-action\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Invoking a trigger or an action\" href=\"#invoking-a-trigger-or-an-action\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eOnce you have the correct auth data, you can test an trigger, a search, or a create action. For example, here's how you invoke a trigger with the key \u003ccode\u003enew_recipe\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"zapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe      # (local mode)\nzapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe -r   # (remote mode)\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe      # (local mode)\nzapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe -r   # (remote mode)\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTo add input data, use the \u003ccode\u003e--inputData\u003c/code\u003e flag (\u003ccode\u003e-i\u003c/code\u003e for short). The input data can come from the command directly, a file, or stdin. See \u003cstrong\u003eEXAMPLES\u003c/strong\u003e below.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWhen you miss any command arguments, such as ACTIONTYPE or ACTIONKEY, the command will prompt you interactively. If you don't want to get interactive prompts, use the \u003ccode\u003e--non-interactive\u003c/code\u003e flag.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--debug\u003c/code\u003e flag will show you the HTTP request logs and any console logs you have in your code.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLimitations in local and relay mode\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-limitations-in-local-and-relay-mode\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Limitations in local and relay mode\" href=\"#limitations-in-local-and-relay-mode\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe following is a non-exhaustive list of current limitations in local and relay mode. We may support them in the future.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eHook triggers, including REST hook subscribe/unsubscribe\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eLine items\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eOutput hydration\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFile upload\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFunction-based connection label\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eBuffered create actions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSearch-or-create actions\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSearch-powered fields\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eautoRefresh for OAuth2 and session auth\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eactionType\u003c/code\u003e | The action type you want to invoke.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eactionKey\u003c/code\u003e | The trigger/action key you want to invoke. If ACTIONTYPE is \"auth\", this can be \"label\", \"refresh\", \"start\", or \"test\".\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-i, --inputData\u003c/code\u003e | The input data to pass to the action. Must be a JSON-encoded object. The data can be passed from the command directly like '{\"key\": \"value\"}', read from a file like @file.json, or read from stdin like @-.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--isFillingDynamicDropdown\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.isFillingDynamicDropdown to true. Only makes sense for a polling trigger. When true in production, this poll is being used to populate a dynamic dropdown.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--isLoadingSample\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.isLoadingSample to true. When true in production, this run is initiated by the user in the Zap editor trying to pull a sample.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--isPopulatingDedupe\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.isPopulatingDedupe to true. Only makes sense for a polling trigger. When true in production, the results of this poll will be used initialize the deduplication list rather than trigger a Zap. This happens when a user enables a Zap.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--limit\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.limit. Only makes sense for a trigger. When used in production, this indicates the number of items you should fetch. -1 means no limit.  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003e-1\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-p, --page\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.page. Only makes sense for a trigger. When used in production, this indicates which page of items you should fetch. First page is 0.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--non-interactive\u003c/code\u003e | Do not show interactive prompts.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-z, --timezone\u003c/code\u003e | Set the default timezone for datetime field interpretation. If not set, defaults to America/Chicago, which matches Zapier production behavior. Find the list timezone names at \u003ca href=\"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tz_database_time_zones\u003c/a\u003e.  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003eAmerica/Chicago\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--redirect-uri\u003c/code\u003e | Only used by \u003ccode\u003eauth start\u003c/code\u003e subcommand. The redirect URI that will be passed to the OAuth2 authorization URL. Usually this should match the one configured in your server's OAuth2 application settings. A local HTTP server will be started to listen for the OAuth2 callback. If your server requires a non-localhost or HTTPS address for the redirect URI, you can set up port forwarding to route the non-localhost or HTTPS address to localhost.  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003ehttp://localhost:9000\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--local-port\u003c/code\u003e | Only used by \u003ccode\u003eauth start\u003c/code\u003e subcommand. The local port that will be used to start the local HTTP server to listen for the OAuth2 callback. This port can be different from the one in the redirect URI if you have port forwarding set up.  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003e9000\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-r, --remote\u003c/code\u003e | Run your trigger/action remotely on Zapier production servers instead of locally. This requires deploying your integration first. Because this (remote) mode uses the same set of API endpoints as the Zap editor and other Zapier products, it allows you to verify exactly how your code will behave in production. Note that \u003ccode\u003e--authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e is required and implied in remote mode, as a production authentication is necessary to invoke in production.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-v, --version\u003c/code\u003e | Only used when \u003ccode\u003e--remote\u003c/code\u003e is set. Specify a deployed version to invoke instead of the one currently set in your local package.json.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-a, --authentication-id\u003c/code\u003e | EXPERIMENTAL: Instead of using the local .env file, use the production authentication data with the given authentication ID (aka the \"app connection\" on Zapier). Find them at \u003ca href=\"https://zapier.com/app/assets/connections\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://zapier.com/app/assets/connections\u003c/a\u003e (\u003ca href=\"https://zpr.io/z8SjFTdnTFZ2\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://zpr.io/z8SjFTdnTFZ2\u003c/a\u003e for instructions) or specify '-' to interactively select one from your available authentications. When specified, the code will still run locally, but all outgoing requests will be proxied through Zapier with the production auth data.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--paging-token\u003c/code\u003e | Set bundle.meta.paging_token. Used for search pagination or bulk reads. When used in production, this indicates which page of items you should fetch.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth start\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth refresh\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth test\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke auth label\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke create add_recipe --inputData '{\"title\": \"Pancakes\"}'\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke search find_recipe -i @file.json --non-interactive\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecat file.json | zapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe -i @-\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke search find_ticket --authentication-id 12345\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke create add_ticket -a -\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe --remote\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke trigger new_recipe -r -a 12345\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier-platform invoke -r -v 2.0.0 -a -\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eLists ongoing migration or promotion jobs for the current integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier jobs\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eA job represents a background process that will be queued up when users execute a \"migrate\" or \"promote\" command for the current integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEach job will be added to the end of a queue of \"promote\" and \"migration\" jobs where the \"Job Stage\" will then be initialized with \"requested\".\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJob stages will then move to \"estimating\", \"in_progress\" and finally one of four \"end\" stages: \"complete\", \"aborted\", \"errored\" or \"paused\".\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJob times will vary as it depends on the size of the queue and how many users your integration has.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJobs are returned from oldest to newest.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-f, --format\u003c/code\u003e | Change the way structured data is presented. If \"json\" or \"raw\", you can pipe the output of the command into other tools, such as jq. One of \u003ccode\u003e[plain | json | raw | row | table]\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003etable\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul your integration as legacy.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier legacy VERSION\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eUse this when an integration version is no longer recommended for new users, but you don't want to block existing users from using it.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eReasons why you might want to mark a version as legacy:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ethis version may be discontinued in the future\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ethis version has bugs\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ea newer version has been released and you want to encourage users to upgrade\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003eversion\u003c/code\u003e | The version to mark as legacy.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier logs\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eLogs are created when your integration is run as part of a Zap. They come from explicit calls to \u003ccode\u003ez.console.log()\u003c/code\u003e, usage of \u003ccode\u003ez.request()\u003c/code\u003e, and any runtime errors.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis won't show logs from running locally with \u003ccode\u003ezapier test\u003c/code\u003e, since those never hit our server.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-v, --version\u003c/code\u003e | Filter logs to the specified version.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-s, --status\u003c/code\u003e | Filter logs to only see errors or successes One of \u003ccode\u003e[any | success | error]\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003eany\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-t, --type\u003c/code\u003e | See logs of the specified type One of \u003ccode\u003e[console | bundle | http]\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003econsole\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--detailed\u003c/code\u003e | See extra info, like request/response body and headers.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-u, --user\u003c/code\u003e | Only show logs for this user. Defaults to your account.  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003eme\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--limit\u003c/code\u003e | Cap the number of logs returned. Max is 50 (also the default)  Defaults to \u003ccode\u003e50\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-f, --format\u003c/code\u003e | Change the way structured data is presented. If \"json\" or \"raw\", you can pipe the output of the command into other tools, such as jq. One of \u003ccode\u003e[plain | json | raw | row | table]\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003etable\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003emigrate\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-migrate\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: migrate\" href=\"#migrate\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMigrate a percentage of users or a single user from one version of your integration to another.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate FROMVERSION TOVERSION [PERCENT]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eStart a migration to move users between different versions of your integration. You may also \"revert\" by simply swapping the from/to verion strings in the command line arguments (i.e. \u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.1 1.0.0\u003c/code\u003e).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eOnly use this command to migrate users between non-breaking versions, use \u003ccode\u003ezapier deprecate\u003c/code\u003e if you have breaking changes!\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMigration time varies based on the number of affected Zaps. Be patient and check \u003ccode\u003ezapier jobs\u003c/code\u003e to track the status. Or use \u003ccode\u003ezapier history\u003c/code\u003e if you want to see older jobs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eSince a migration is only for non-breaking changes, users are not emailed about the update/migration. It will be a transparent process for them.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eWe recommend migrating a small subset of users first, via the percent argument, then watching error logs of the new version for any sort of odd behavior. When you feel confident there are no bugs, go ahead and migrate everyone. If you see unexpected errors, you can revert.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can migrate a specific user's Zaps by using \u003ccode\u003e--user\u003c/code\u003e (i.e. \u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.0 1.0.1 --user=user@example.com\u003c/code\u003e). This will migrate Zaps that are private for that user. Zaps that are\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496277647629\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eshared across the team\u003c/a\u003e,\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ca href=\"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/8496326497037-Share-app-connections-with-your-team\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eshared app connections\u003c/a\u003e, or\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003ein a \u003ca href=\"https://help.zapier.com/hc/en-us/articles/22330977078157-Collaborate-with-members-of-your-Team-or-Company-account\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eteam/company account\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ewill \u003cstrong\u003enot\u003c/strong\u003e be migrated.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAlternatively, you can pass the \u003ccode\u003e--account\u003c/code\u003e flag, (i.e. \u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.0 1.0.1 --account=account@example.com\u003c/code\u003e). This will migrate all Zaps owned by the user, Private \u0026amp; Shared, within all accounts for which the specified user is a member.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThe \u003ccode\u003e--account\u003c/code\u003e flag should be used cautiously as it can break shared Zaps for other users in Team or Enterprise accounts.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou cannot pass both \u003ccode\u003ePERCENT\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e--user\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003e--account\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou cannot pass both \u003ccode\u003e--user\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003e--account\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003efromVersion\u003c/code\u003e | The version FROM which to migrate users.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003etoVersion\u003c/code\u003e | The version TO which to migrate users.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003epercent\u003c/code\u003e | Percentage (between 1 and 100) of users to migrate.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--user\u003c/code\u003e | Migrates a user's private Zaps under the user's individual account, excluding organization accounts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--account\u003c/code\u003e | Migrates a user's private and shared Zaps under the user's individual and organization accounts\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-y, --yes\u003c/code\u003e | Automatically answer \"yes\" to any prompts. Useful if you want to avoid interactive prompts to run this command in CI.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.0 1.0.1\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.1 2.0.0 10\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 2.0.0 2.0.1 --user=user@example.com\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 2.0.0 2.0.1 --account=account@example.com\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePromote a specific version to public access.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier promote VERSION\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePromote an integration version into production (non-private) rotation, which means new users can use this integration version.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThis \u003cstrong\u003edoes\u003c/strong\u003e mark the version as the official public version - all other versions \u0026amp; users are grandfathered.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThis does \u003cstrong\u003eNOT\u003c/strong\u003e build/upload or deploy a version to Zapier - you should \u003ccode\u003ezapier push\u003c/code\u003e first.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThis does \u003cstrong\u003eNOT\u003c/strong\u003e move old users over to this version - \u003ccode\u003ezapier migrate 1.0.0 1.0.1\u003c/code\u003e does that.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eThis does \u003cstrong\u003eNOT\u003c/strong\u003e recommend old users stop using this version - \u003ccode\u003ezapier deprecate 1.0.0 2017-01-01\u003c/code\u003e does that.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003ePromotes are an inherently safe operation for all existing users of your integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAfter a promotion, go to your developer platform to \u003ca href=\"https://platform.zapier.com/manage/user-feedback#3-close-resolved-issues\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eclose issues that were resolved\u003c/a\u003e in the updated version.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eIf your integration is private and passes our integration checks, this will give you a URL to a form where you can fill in additional information for your integration to go public. After reviewing, the Zapier team will approve to make it public if there are no issues or decline with feedback.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCheck \u003ccode\u003ezapier jobs\u003c/code\u003e to track the status of the promotion. Or use \u003ccode\u003ezapier history\u003c/code\u003e if you want to see older jobs.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003eversion\u003c/code\u003e | The version you want to promote.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-y, --yes\u003c/code\u003e | Automatically answer \"yes\" to any prompts. Useful if you want to avoid interactive prompts to run this command in CI.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier promote 1.0.0\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003epull\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-pull\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: pull\" href=\"#pull\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRetrieve and update your local integration files with the promoted version (or latest version if not public).\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier pull\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis command updates your local integration files with the promoted version (or latest version if not public). You will be prompted with a confirmation dialog before continuing if there any destructive file changes.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eZapier may release new versions of your integration with bug fixes or new features. In the event this occurs, you will be unable to do the following until your local files are updated by running \u003ccode\u003ezapier pull\u003c/code\u003e:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003epush to the promoted version\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003epromote a new version\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003emigrate users from one version to another\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier push\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis command is the same as running \u003ccode\u003ezapier build\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ezapier upload\u003c/code\u003e in sequence. See those for more info.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--disable-dependency-detection\u003c/code\u003e | Disable \"smart\" file inclusion. By default, Zapier only includes files that are required by your entry point (\u003ccode\u003eindex.js\u003c/code\u003e by default). If you (or your dependencies) require files dynamically (such as with \u003ccode\u003erequire(someVar)\u003c/code\u003e), then you may see \"Cannot find module\" errors. Disabling this may make your \u003ccode\u003ebuild.zip\u003c/code\u003e too large. If that's the case, try using the \u003ccode\u003eincludeInBuild\u003c/code\u003e option in your \u003ccode\u003e.zapierapprc\u003c/code\u003e. See the docs about \u003ccode\u003eincludeInBuild\u003c/code\u003e for more info.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--skip-dep-install\u003c/code\u003e | [alias: --skip-npm-install]\nSkips installing a fresh copy of dependencies for shorter build time. Helpful for using yarn, pnpm, or local copies of dependencies.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--snapshot\u003c/code\u003e | Pass in a label to create a snapshot version of this integration for development and testing purposes. The version will be created as: 0.0.0-MY-LABEL\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier push\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier push --snapshot MY-LABEL\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch2 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eregister\u003c/h2\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-register\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: register\" href=\"#register\"\u003e\u003csvg class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cblockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRegister a new integration in your account, or update the existing one if a \u003ccode\u003e.zapierapprc\u003c/code\u003e file is found.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier register [TITLE]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis command creates a new integration and links it in the \u003ccode\u003e./.zapierapprc\u003c/code\u003e file. If \u003ccode\u003e.zapierapprc\u003c/code\u003e already exists, it will ask you if you want to update the currently-linked integration, as opposed to creating a new one.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eAfter registering a new integration, you can run \u003ccode\u003ezapier push\u003c/code\u003e to build and upload your integration for use in the Zapier editor. This will change \u003ccode\u003e.zapierapprc\u003c/code\u003e, which identifies this directory as holding code for a specific integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003etitle\u003c/code\u003e | Your integration's public title. Asked interactively if not present.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-D, --desc\u003c/code\u003e | A sentence describing your app in 140 characters or less, e.g. \"Trello is a team collaboration tool to organize tasks and keep projects on track.\"\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-u, --url\u003c/code\u003e | The homepage URL of your app, e.g., \u003ca href=\"https://example.com\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003ehttps://example.com\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-a, --audience\u003c/code\u003e | Are you building a public or private integration?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-r, --role\u003c/code\u003e | What is your relationship with the app you're integrating with Zapier?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-c, --category\u003c/code\u003e | How would you categorize your app? Choose the most appropriate option for your app's core features.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-s, --subscribe\u003c/code\u003e | Get tips and recommendations about this integration along with our monthly newsletter that details the performance of your integration and the latest Zapier news.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-y, --yes\u003c/code\u003e | Assume yes for all yes/no prompts. This flag will also update an existing integration (as opposed to registering a new one) if a .zapierapprc file is found.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul Integration\"\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier register \"My Cool Integration\" --desc \"My Cool Integration helps you integrate your apps with the apps that you need.\" --no-subscribe\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier register \"My Cool Integration\" --url \"https://www.zapier.com\" --audience private --role employee integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier scaffold ACTIONTYPE NOUN\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe first argument should be one of \u003ccode\u003etrigger|search|create|resource\u003c/code\u003e followed by the noun that this will act on (something like \"contact\" or \"deal\").\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThe scaffold command does two general things:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCreates a new file (such as \u003ccode\u003etriggers/contact.js\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eImports and registers it inside your \u003ccode\u003eindex.js\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eYou can mix and match several options to customize the created scaffold for your project.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003eactionType\u003c/code\u003e | undefined\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003enoun\u003c/code\u003e | undefined\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --dest\u003c/code\u003e | Specify the new file's directory. Use this flag when you want to create a different folder structure such as \u003ccode\u003esrc/triggers\u003c/code\u003e instead of the default \u003ccode\u003etriggers\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003e[triggers|searches|creates]/{noun}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--test-dest\u003c/code\u003e | Specify the new test file's directory. Use this flag when you want to create a different folder structure such as \u003ccode\u003esrc/triggers\u003c/code\u003e instead of the default \u003ccode\u003etriggers\u003c/code\u003e. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003etest/[triggers|searches|creates]/{noun}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-e, --entry\u003c/code\u003e | Supply the path to your integration's entry point (\u003ccode\u003eindex.js\u003c/code\u003e or \u003ccode\u003esrc/index.ts\u003c/code\u003e). This will try to automatically detect the correct file if not provided.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-f, --force\u003c/code\u003e | Should we overwrite an existing trigger/search/create file?\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e--no-help\u003c/code\u003e | When scaffolding, should we skip adding helpful intro comments? Useful if this isn't your first rodeo.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e-d, --debug\u003c/code\u003e | Show extra debugging output.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eExamples\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier scaffold trigger contact\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier scaffold search contact --dest=my_src/searches\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier scaffold create contact --entry=src/index.js\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ezapier scaffold resource contact integration.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eUsage\u003c/strong\u003e: \u003ccode\u003ezapier team:add EMAIL ROLE [MESSAGE]\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThese users come in three levels:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003eadmin\u003c/code\u003e, who can edit everything about the integration\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecollaborator\u003c/code\u003e, who has read-only access for the app, and will receive periodic email updates. These updates include quarterly health scores and more.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003esubscriber\u003c/code\u003e, who can't directly access the app, but will receive periodic email updates. These updates include quarterly health scores and more.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eTeam members can be freely added and removed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eArguments\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003eemail\u003c/code\u003e | The user to be invited. If they don't have a Zapier account, they'll be prompted to create one.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e(required) \u003ccode\u003erole\u003c/code\u003e | The level the invited team member should be at. Admins can edit everything and get email updates. Collaborators have read-access to the app and get email updates. Subscribers only get email updates.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003emessage\u003c/code\u003e | A message sent in the email to your team member, if you need to provide context. Wrap the message in quotes to ensure spaces get saved.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFlags\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul
