EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eperform\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ca href=\"#requestschema\"\u003e/RequestSchema\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like \u003ccode\u003e(z) =\u0026gt; [{id: 123}]\u003c/code\u003e or a request like \u003ccode\u003e{url: 'http...'}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat should the form a user sees and configures look like?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFieldGroups\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldgroupsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldGroupsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDefines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#outputfieldsschema\"\u003e/OutputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e (with exceptions, see description)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if \u003ccode\u003edisplay.hidden\u003c/code\u003e is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elock\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#lockobjectschema\"\u003e/LockObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eZapier uses this configuration to ensure this action is performed one at a time per scope (avoid concurrency).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ethrottle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#throttleobjectschema\"\u003e/ThrottleObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eZapier uses this configuration to apply throttling when the limit for the window is exceeded.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecleanInputData\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIf true, Zapier removes empty strings, \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eundefined\u003c/code\u003e, and empty Arrays or objects from \u003ccode\u003ebundle.inputData\u003c/code\u003e recursively before passing it to your \u003ccode\u003eperform*\u003c/code\u003e function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. There is also a global flag with the same name in \u003ccode\u003eApp.flags\u003c/code\u003e. This one takes precedence over the global one.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" href=\"#keyschema\"\u003e/KeySchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOptionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eperform\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ca href=\"#requestschema\"\u003e/RequestSchema\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like \u003ccode\u003e(z) =\u0026gt; [{id: 123}]\u003c/code\u003e or a request like \u003ccode\u003e{url: 'http...'}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecanPaginate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDoes this endpoint support pagination via temporary cursor storage?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat should the form a user sees and configures look like?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFieldGroups\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldgroupsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldGroupsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDefines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#outputfieldsschema\"\u003e/OutputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e (with exceptions, see description)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat does a sample of data look like? href=\"#keyschema\"\u003e/KeySchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eOptionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eperform\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ca href=\"#requestschema\"\u003e/RequestSchema\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like \u003ccode\u003e(z) =\u0026gt; [{id: 123}]\u003c/code\u003e or a request like \u003ccode\u003e{url: 'http...'}\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eperformResume\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA function that parses data from a perform (which uses z.generateCallbackUrl()) and callback request to resume this action.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eperformGet\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ca href=\"#requestschema\"\u003e/RequestSchema\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eHow will Zapier get a single record? If you find yourself reaching for this - consider resources and their built-in get methods.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecanPaginate\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDoes this search support pagination?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat should the form a user sees and configures look like?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFieldGroups\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#inputfieldgroupsschema\"\u003e/InputFieldGroupsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDefines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#outputfieldsschema\"\u003e/OutputFieldsSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e (with exceptions, see description)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eWhat does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if \u003ccode\u003edisplay.hidden\u003c/code\u003e is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elock\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#lockobjectschema\"\u003e/LockObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eZapier uses this configuration to ensure this action is performed one at a time per scope (avoid concurrency).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ethrottle\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#throttleobjectschema\"\u003e/ThrottleObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eZapier uses this configuration to apply throttling when the limit for the window is exceeded.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecleanInputData\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIf true, Zapier removes empty strings, \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eundefined\u003c/code\u003e, and empty Arrays or objects from \u003ccode\u003ebundle.inputData\u003c/code\u003e recursively before passing it to your \u003ccode\u003eperform*\u003c/code\u003e function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. There is also a global flag with the same name in \u003ccode\u003eApp.flags\u003c/code\u003e. This one takes precedence over the global one.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" key to use for locking. This should be unique to the operation. While actions of different integrations with the same key and scope will never lock each other out, actions of the same integration with the same key and scope will do. User data provided for the input fields can be used in the key with the use of the curly braces referencing. For example, to access the user data provided for the input field \"test_field\", use \u003ccode\u003e{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}\u003c/code\u003e. Note that a required input field should be referenced to get user data always.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escope\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'user'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'auth'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'account'\u003c/code\u003e)]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eBy default, locks are scoped to the app. That is, all users of the app will share the same locks. If you want to restrict serial access to a specific user, auth, or account, you can set the scope to one or more of the following: 'user' - Locks based on user ids.  'auth' - Locks based on unique auth ids. 'account' - Locks for all users under a single account. You may also combine scopes. Note that \"app\" is included, always, in the scope provided. For example, a scope of ['account', 'auth'] would result to ['app', 'account', 'auth'].\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etimeout\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einteger\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe number of seconds to hold the lock before releasing it to become accessible to other task invokes that need it. If not provided, the default set by the app will be used. It cannot be more than 180.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" unique machine readable key for this value (IE: \"fname\").\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elabel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA human readable label for this value (IE: \"First Name\").\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'string'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'text'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'integer'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'number'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'boolean'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'datetime'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'file'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'password'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'copy'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'code'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'json'\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe type of this value. Use \u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e for basic text input, \u003ccode\u003etext\u003c/code\u003e for a large, \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;textarea\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e style box, and \u003ccode\u003ecode\u003c/code\u003e for a \u003ccode\u003e\u0026lt;textarea\u0026gt;\u003c/code\u003e with a fixed-width font. Field type of \u003ccode\u003efile\u003c/code\u003e will accept either a file object or a string. If a URL is provided in the string, Zapier will automatically make a GET for that file. Otherwise, a .txt file will be generated.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erequired\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIf this value is required or not.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edefault\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA default value that is saved the first time a Zap is created.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elist\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eActs differently when used in inputFields vs. when used in outputFields. In inputFields: Can a user provide multiples of this field? In outputFields: Does this field return an array of items of type \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003echildren\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ca href=\"#plaininputfieldschema\"\u003e/PlainInputFieldSchema\u003c/a\u003e]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn array of child fields that define the structure of a sub-object for this field. Usually used for line items.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIs this field a key/value input?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ehelpText\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA human readable description of this value (IE: \"The first part of a full name.\"). You can use Markdown.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esearch\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#refresourceschema\"\u003e/RefResourceSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA reference to a search that will guide the user to add a search step to populate this field when creating a Zap.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edynamic\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#refresourceschema\"\u003e/RefResourceSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA reference to a trigger that will power a dynamic dropdown.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edependsOn\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eSpecifies which other input fields this field depends on. These must be filled before this one becomes enabled, and when their values change, this field's value should be cleared.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eresource\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eExplicitly links this input field to a resource. Use the resource key (e.g., \"spreadsheet\") or dot notation for resource fields (e.g., \"spreadsheet.url\"). If not set for dynamic dropdowns, the resource is derived implicitly from the \u003ccode\u003edynamic\u003c/code\u003e property.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003echoices\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ca href=\"#fieldchoicesschema\"\u003e/FieldChoicesSchema\u003c/a\u003e, \u003ca href=\"#fielddynamicchoicesschema\"\u003e/FieldDynamicChoicesSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDescribes how to populate this dropdown. Can be a static list or a dynamic object with pagination and search support.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eplaceholder\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn example value that is not saved.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ealtersDynamicFields\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eDoes the value of this field affect the definitions of other fields in the set?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ecomputed\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIs this field automatically populated (and hidden from the user)? Note: Only OAuth, Session Auth, and certain internal use cases support fields with this key.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einputFormat\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUseful when you expect the input to be part of a longer string. Put \"{{input}}\" in place of the user's input (IE: \"https://{{input}}.yourdomain.com\").\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emeta\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#fieldmetaschema\"\u003e/FieldMetaSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAllows for additional metadata to be stored on the field. Supports simple key-values only (no sub-objects or arrays).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003egroup\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#keyschema\"\u003e/KeySchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eReferences a group key from the operation's inputFieldGroups to organize this field with others.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eschema\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#jsonschemaschema\"\u003e/JsonSchemaSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA JSON Schema object that describes the expected structure of the JSON value. Only valid when \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e is array, must be of either string or FieldChoiceWithLabelSchema)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{ key: 'abc', choices: [ { label: 'Red', value: '#f00' } ] }\u003c/code\u003e - \u003cem\u003eInvalid value for key: choices (if an array of FieldChoiceWithLabelSchema, must provide key \u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{ key: 'abc', choices: 'mobile' }\u003c/code\u003e - \u003cem\u003eInvalid value for key: choices (must be either object or array)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{ key: 'abc', type: 'string', schema: { type: 'object' } }\u003c/code\u003e - \u003cem\u003eschema is only valid when type is json\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{ key: 'abc', type: 'json', schema: { type: 'foobar' } }\u003c/code\u003e - \u003cem\u003eschema must contain a valid JSON Schema (invalid type)\u003c/em\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003ccode\u003e{ key: 'abc', children: [ '$func$2$f$' ] }\u003c/code\u003e - \u003cem\u003eInvalid value for key: unique machine readable key for this value (IE: \"fname\").\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elabel\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA human readable label for this value (IE: \"First Name\").\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'string'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'number'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'boolean'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'datetime'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'file'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'password'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'integer'\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe type of this value. Field type of \u003ccode\u003efile\u003c/code\u003e will accept either a file object or a string. If a URL is provided in the string, Zapier will automatically make a GET for that file. Otherwise, a .txt file will be generated.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003erequired\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIf this value is required or not.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edefault\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA default value that is saved the first time a Zap is created.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elist\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eActs differently when used in inputFields vs. when used in outputFields. In inputFields: Can a user provide multiples of this field? In outputFields: Does this field return an array of items of type \u003ccode\u003etype\u003c/code\u003e?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003echildren\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ca href=\"#plainoutputfieldschema\"\u003e/PlainOutputFieldSchema\u003c/a\u003e]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn array of child fields that define the structure of a sub-object for this field. Usually used for line items.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003edict\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIs this field a key/value input?\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eprimary\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eUse this field as part of the primary key for deduplication. You can set multiple fields as \"primary\", provided they are unique together. If no fields are set, Zapier will default to using the \u003ccode\u003eid\u003c/code\u003e field. \u003ccode\u003eprimary\u003c/code\u003e only makes sense for \u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e. It only works in static \u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e; will not work in custom/dynamic \u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e. For more information, see \u003ca href=\"https://platform.zapier.com/build/deduplication\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eHow deduplication works in Zapier\u003c/a\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esteadyState\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003ePrevents triggering on new output until all values for fields with this property remain unchanged for 2 polls. It can be used to, e.g., not trigger on a new contact until the contact has completed typing their name. NOTE that this only applies to the \u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e of polling triggers.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enumber\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn example value for this field. Can be any type (string, number, boolean, object, array, null) to match the expected field output. Values provided here will be combined with values in the operation level \u003ccode\u003esample\u003c/code\u003e field, with this field taking precedence. This is most useful when using a function to generate dynamic \u003ccode\u003eoutputFields\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cmarkdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\u003ctable\u003e\n\u003cthead\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eKey\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eRequired\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eType\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003cth\u003eDescription\u003c/th\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/thead\u003e\n\u003ctbody\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003emethod\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'GET'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'PUT'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'POST'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'PATCH'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'DELETE'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'HEAD'\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe HTTP method for the request.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eurl\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA URL for the request (we will parse the querystring and merge with params). Keys and values will not be re-encoded.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ebody\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eCan be nothing, a raw string or JSON (object or array).\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eparams\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#flatobjectschema\"\u003e/FlatObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA mapping of the querystring - will get merged with any query params in the URL. Keys and values will be encoded.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eheaders\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#flatobjectschema\"\u003e/FlatObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe HTTP headers for the request.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eauth\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eoneOf(\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e], \u003ca href=\"#flatobjectschema\"\u003e/FlatObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAn object holding the auth parameters for OAuth1 request signing, like \u003ccode\u003e{oauth_token: 'abcd', oauth_token_secret: '1234'}\u003c/code\u003e. Or an array reserved (i.e. not implemented yet) to hold the username and password for Basic Auth. Like \u003ccode\u003e['AzureDiamond', 'hunter2']\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eremoveMissingValuesFrom\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eobject\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eShould missing values be sent? (empty strings, \u003ccode\u003enull\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003eundefined\u003c/code\u003e only — \u003ccode\u003e[]\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e{}\u003c/code\u003e, and \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e will still be sent). Allowed fields are \u003ccode\u003eparams\u003c/code\u003e and \u003ccode\u003ebody\u003c/code\u003e. The default is \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e, ex: \u003ccode\u003eremoveMissingValuesFrom: { params: false, body: false }\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eserializeValueForCurlies\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ca href=\"#functionschema\"\u003e/FunctionSchema\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eA function to customize how to serialize a value for curlies \u003ccode\u003e{{var}}\u003c/code\u003e in the request object. By default, when this is unspecified, the request client only replaces curlies where variables are strings, and would throw an error for non-strings. The function should accepts a single argument as the value to be serialized and return the string representation of the argument.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eskipThrowForStatus\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eIf \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e, don't throw an exception for response 400 \u0026lt;= status \u0026lt; 600 automatically before resolving with the response. Defaults to \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eskipEncodingChars\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eContains the characters that you want left unencoded in the query params (\u003ccode\u003ereq.params\u003c/code\u003e). If unspecified, \u003ccode\u003ez.request()\u003c/code\u003e will percent-encode non-ascii characters and these reserved characters: \u003ccode\u003e:$/?#[]@$\u0026amp;+,;=^@`\\\u003c/code\u003e.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv The number of invocations begins at zero at the start of each window.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elimit\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einteger\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe maximum number of invocations for an action, allowed within the timeframe window.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003ekey\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe key to throttle with in combination with the scope. User data provided for the input fields can be used in the key with the use of the curly braces referencing. For example, to access the user data provided for the input field \"test_field\", use \u003ccode\u003e{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}\u003c/code\u003e. Note that a required input field should be referenced to get user data always.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003escope\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'user'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'auth'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'account'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'action'\u003c/code\u003e)]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe granularity to throttle by. You can set the scope to one or more of the following: 'user' - Throttles based on user ids.  'auth' - Throttles based on auth ids. 'account' - Throttles based on account ids for all users under a single account. 'action' - Throttles the action it is set on separately from other actions. By default, throttling is scoped to the action and account.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eretry\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe effect of throttling on the tasks of the action. \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e means throttled tasks are automatically retried after some delay, while \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e means tasks are held without retry. It defaults to \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e. NOTE that it has no effect on polling triggers and should not be set.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003efilter\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'free'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'trial'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'paid'\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEXPERIMENTAL: Account-based attribute to override the throttle by. You can set to one of the following: \"free\", \"trial\", \"paid\". Therefore, the throttle scope would be automatically set to \"account\" and ONLY the accounts based on the specified filter will have their requests throttled based on the throttle overrides while the rest are throttled based on the original configuration.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eoverrides\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003earray\u003c/code\u003e[\u003ca href=\"#throttleoverrideobjectschema\"\u003e/ThrottleOverrideObjectSchema\u003c/a\u003e]\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eEXPERIMENTAL: Overrides the original throttle configuration based on a Zapier account attribute.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch4 timeframe, in seconds, within which the system tracks the number of invocations for an action. The number of invocations begins at zero at the start of each window.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003elimit\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003einteger\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe maximum number of invocations for an action, allowed within the timeframe window.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003efilter\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eyes\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003estring\u003c/code\u003e in (\u003ccode\u003e'free'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'trial'\u003c/code\u003e, \u003ccode\u003e'paid'\u003c/code\u003e)\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eAccount-based attribute to override the throttle by. You can set to one of the following: \"free\", \"trial\", \"paid\". Therefore, the throttle scope would be automatically set to \"account\" and ONLY the accounts based on the specified filter will have their requests throttled based on the throttle overrides while the rest are throttled based on the original configuration.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003ctr\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eretry\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eno\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003e\u003ccode\u003eboolean\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003ctd\u003eThe effect of throttling on the tasks of the action. \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e means throttled tasks are automatically retried after some delay, while \u003ccode\u003efalse\u003c/code\u003e means tasks are held without retry. It defaults to \u003ccode\u003etrue\u003c/code\u003e. NOTE that it has no effect on polling triggers and should not be set.\u003c/td\u003e\n\u003c/tr\u003e\n\u003c/tbody\u003e\n\u003c/table\u003e\u003c/markdown-accessiblity-table\u003e\n\u003cdiv Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/AppFlagsSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`skipHttpPatch` | no | `boolean` | By default, Zapier patches the core `http` module so that all requests (including those from 3rd-party SDKs) can be logged. Set this to true if you're seeing issues using an SDK (such as AWS).","`skipThrowForStatus` | no | `boolean` | Starting in `core` version `10.0.0`, `response.throwForStatus()` was called by default. We introduced a per-request way to opt-out of this behavior. This flag takes that a step further and controls that behavior integration-wide **for requests made using `z.request()`**. Unless they specify otherwise (per-request, or via middleware), [Shorthand requests](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/README.md#shorthand-http-requests) _always_ call `throwForStatus()`. `z.request()` calls can also ignore this flag if they set `skipThrowForStatus` directly. It is important to note that for oauth2 or session auths with `authRefresh:true`, `401` status codes will throw a `RefreshAuthError` regardless of `skipThrowForStatus`, and will need to be handled manually if intervention is required.","`throwForThrottlingEarly` | no | `boolean` | Starting in `core` version `18.0.0`, 429 (throttling) responses throw a `ThrottledError` before `afterResponse` middleware runs by default. Set this flag to `true` to preserve the old behavior where `afterResponse` middleware can see and handle 429 responses. This flag can be overridden per-request by setting `throwForThrottlingEarly` directly on the request options.","`cleanInputData` | no | `boolean` | If true, Zapier removes empty strings, `null`, `undefined`, and empty Arrays or objects from `bundle.inputData` recursively before passing it to your `perform*` function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. This is a global flag that affects all the triggers and actions in your integration. The `cleanInputData` flag in `operation` takes precedence over this one.","","#### Examples","","* `{ skipHttpPatch: true, skipThrowForStatus: false, throwForThrottlingEarly: true }`","* `{ skipHttpPatch: false, skipThrowForStatus: true, throwForThrottlingEarly: false }`","* `{ throwForThrottlingEarly: true }`","* `{}`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{ foo: true }` - _Invalid key._","* `{ skipHttpPatch: 'yes' }` - _Invalid value._","* `{ skipThrowForStatus: 'no' }` - _Invalid value._","* `{ throwForThrottlingEarly: 'yes' }` - _Invalid value._","","-----","","## Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/AppSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`version` | **yes** | [/VersionSchema](#versionschema) | A version identifier for your code.","`platformVersion` | **yes** | [/VersionSchema](#versionschema) | A version identifier for the Zapier execution environment.","`beforeApp` | no | [/MiddlewaresSchema](#middlewaresschema) | EXPERIMENTAL: Before the perform method is called on your app, you can modify the execution context.","`afterApp` | no | [/MiddlewaresSchema](#middlewaresschema) | EXPERIMENTAL: After the perform method is called on your app, you can modify the response.","`authentication` | no | [/AuthenticationSchema](#authenticationschema) | Choose what scheme your API uses for authentication.","`requestTemplate` | no | [/RequestSchema](#requestschema) | Define a request mixin, great for setting custom headers, content-types, etc.","`beforeRequest` | no | [/MiddlewaresSchema](#middlewaresschema) | Before an HTTP request is sent via our `z.request()` client, you can modify it.","`afterResponse` | no | [/MiddlewaresSchema](#middlewaresschema) | After an HTTP response is recieved via our `z.request()` client, you can modify it.","`hydrators` | no | [/HydratorsSchema](#hydratorsschema) | An optional bank of named functions that you can use in `z.hydrate('someName')` to lazily load data.","`resources` | no | [/ResourcesSchema](#resourcesschema) | All the resources for your app. Zapier will take these and generate the relevent triggers/searches/creates automatically.","`triggers` | no | [/TriggersSchema](#triggersschema) | All the triggers for your app. You can add your own here, or Zapier will automatically register any from the list/hook methods on your resources.","`bulkReads` | no | [/BulkReadsSchema](#bulkreadsschema) | All of the read bulks (GETs) your app exposes to retrieve resources in batches.","`searches` | no | [/SearchesSchema](#searchesschema) | All the searches for your app. You can add your own here, or Zapier will If a primitive is needed, use `type: 'string'` on the input field directly_","","-----","","## /KeySchema","","A unique identifier for this item.","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `string`","* **Pattern** - `^[a-zA-Z]+[a-zA-Z0-9_]*$`","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/KeySchema.js)","","","#### Examples","","* `'vk'`","* `'validKey'`","* `'ValidKey'`","* `'Valid_Key_2'`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `''` - _Cannot be empty_","* `'A'` - _Minimum of two characters_","* `'1_Key'` - _Must start with a letter_","* `'a-Key'` - _Must not use dashes_","","-----","","## /LockObjectSchema","","Zapier uses this configuration to ensure this action is performed one at a time per scope (avoid concurrency).","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `object`","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/LockObjectSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`key` | **yes** | `string` | The key to use for locking. This should be unique to the operation. While actions of different integrations with the same key and scope will never lock each other out, actions of the same integration with the same key and scope will do. User data provided for the input fields can be used in the key with the use of the curly braces referencing. For example, to access the user data provided for the input field \"test_field\", use `{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}`. Note that a required input field should be referenced to get user data always.","`scope` | no | `array`[`string` in (`'user'`, `'auth'`, `'account'`)] | By default, locks are scoped to the app. That is, all users of the app will share the same locks. If you want to restrict serial access to a specific user, auth, or account, you can set the scope to one or more of the following: 'user' - Locks based on user ids.  'auth' - Locks based on unique auth ids. 'account' - Locks for all users under a single account. You may also combine scopes. Note that \"app\" is included, always, in the scope provided. For example, a scope of ['account', 'auth'] would result to ['app', 'account', 'auth'].","`timeout` | no | `integer` | The number of seconds to hold the lock before releasing it to become accessible to other task invokes that need it. If not provided, the default set by the app will be used. It cannot be more than 180.","","#### Examples","","* `{ key: 'random_key', scope: [ 'account', 'user' ], timeout: 30 }`","* `{ key: '{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}' }`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{ key: 'random_key', scope: [ 'zap' ] }` - _Invalid scope provided: `zap`._","* `{}` - _Missing required key: `key`._","","-----","","## /MiddlewaresSchema","","List of before or after middlewares. Can be an array of functions or a single function","","#### Details","","* **Type** - oneOf(`array`[[/FunctionSchema](#functionschema)], [/FunctionSchema](#functionschema))","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/MiddlewaresSchema.js)","","","#### Examples","","* `{ require: 'some/path/to/file.js' }`","* `[ { require: 'some/path/to/file.js' } ]`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{}` - _Does not match either /FunctionSchema or an array of such_","","-----","","## /OutputFieldsSchema","","An array or collection of output fields.","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `array`[oneOf([/PlainOutputFieldSchema](#plainoutputfieldschema), [/FunctionSchema](#functionschema))]","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/OutputFieldsSchema.js)","","","#### Examples","","* `[ { key: 'abc' } ]`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{}` - _Must be an array_","","-----","","## /PlainInputFieldSchema","","Field schema specialized for input fields. In addition to the requirements below, the following keys are mutually exclusive:","","* `children` \u0026 `list`","* `children` \u0026 `dict`","* `children` \u0026 `type`","* `children` \u0026 `placeholder`","* `children` \u0026 `helpText`","* `children` \u0026 `default`","* `dict` \u0026 `list`","* `dynamic` \u0026 `dict`","* `dynamic` \u0026 `choices`","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `object`","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/PlainInputFieldSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`key` | **yes** | `string` | A unique machine readable key for this value (IE: \"fname\").","`label` | no | `string` | A human readable label for this value (IE: \"First Name\").","`type` | no | `string` in (`'string'`, `'text'`, `'integer'`, `'number'`, `'boolean'`, `'datetime'`, `'file'`, `'password'`, `'copy'`, `'code'`, `'json'`) | The type of this value. Use `string` for basic text input, `text` for a large, `\u003ctextarea\u003e` style box, and `code` for a `\u003ctextarea\u003e` with a fixed-width font. Field type of `file` will accept either a file object or a string. If a URL is provided in the string, Zapier will automatically make a GET for that file. Otherwise, a .txt file will be generated.","`required` | no | `boolean` | If this value is required or not.","`default` | no | `string` | A default value that is saved the first time a Zap is created.","`list` | no | `boolean` | Acts differently when used in inputFields vs. when used in outputFields. In outputFields: Does this field return an array of items of type `type`?","`children` | no | `array`[[/PlainInputFieldSchema](#plaininputfieldschema)] | An array of child fields that define the structure of a sub-object for this field. Only valid when `type` is `json`.","","#### Examples","","* `{ key: 'abc' }`","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: { mobile: 'Mobile Phone' } }`","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: [ 'first', 'second', 'third' ] }`","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: [ { label: 'Red', sample: '#f00', value: '#f00' } ] }`","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: { perform: '$func$0$f$' } }`","* `{ key: 'abc', children: [ { key: 'abc' } ] }`","* `{ key: 'abc', type: 'integer' }`","* ```","  {","    key: 'abc',","    type: 'integer',","    meta: { internalType: 'numeric', should_call_api: true, display_order: 1 }","  }","  ```","* `{ key: 'name', group: 'contact' }`","* `{ key: 'email', group: 'contact' }`","* ```","  {","    key: 'payload',","    type: 'json',","    schema: { type: 'object', properties: { name: { type: 'string' } } }","  }","  ```","* `{ key: 'spreadsheet', dependsOn: [ 'folder' ] }`","* `{ key: 'worksheet', dependsOn: [ 'folder', 'spreadsheet' ] }`","* `{ key: 'spreadsheet_id', resource: 'spreadsheet', choices: { perform: '$func$0$f$' } }`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{}` - _Missing required key: key_","* `{ key: 'abc', type: 'loltype' }` - _Invalid value for key: type_","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: {} }` - _Invalid value for key: choices (cannot be empty)_","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: [] }` - _Invalid value for key: choices (cannot be empty)_","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: [ 3 ] }` - _Invalid value for key: choices (if an array, must be of either string or FieldChoiceWithLabelSchema)_","* `{ key: 'abc', choices: [ { label: 'Red', value: '#f00' } ] }` - Keys and values will be encoded.","`headers` | no | [/FlatObjectSchema](#flatobjectschema) | The HTTP headers for the request.","`auth` | no | oneOf(`array`[`string`], [/FlatObjectSchema](#flatobjectschema)) | An object holding the auth parameters for OAuth1 request signing, like `{oauth_token: 'abcd', oauth_token_secret: '1234'}`. The function should accepts a single argument as the value to be serialized and return the string representation of the argument.","`skipThrowForStatus` | no | `boolean` | If `true`, don't throw an exception for response 400 \u003c= status \u003c 600 automatically before resolving with the response. To share a limit across multiple actions in an integration, each should have the same configuration set without \"action\" in the scope.","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `object`","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/ThrottleObjectSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`window` | **yes** | `integer` | The timeframe, in seconds, within which the system tracks the number of invocations for an action. The number of invocations begins at zero at the start of each window.","`limit` | **yes** | `integer` | The maximum number of invocations for an action, allowed within the timeframe window.","`key` | no | `string` | The key to throttle with in combination with the scope. User data provided for the input fields can be used in the key with the use of the curly braces referencing. For example, to access the user data provided for the input field \"test_field\", use `{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}`. Note that a required input field should be referenced to get user data always.","`scope` | no | `array`[`string` in (`'user'`, `'auth'`, `'account'`, `'action'`)] | The granularity to throttle by. You can set the scope to one or more of the following: 'user' - Throttles based on user ids.  'auth' - Throttles based on auth ids. 'account' - Throttles based on account ids for all users under a single account. 'action' - Throttles the action it is set on separately from other actions. By default, throttling is scoped to the action and account.","`retry` | no | `boolean` | The effect of throttling on the tasks of the action. `true` means throttled tasks are automatically retried after some delay, while `false` means tasks are held without retry. It defaults to `true`. NOTE that it has no effect on polling triggers and should not be set.","`filter` | no | `string` in (`'free'`, `'trial'`, `'paid'`) | EXPERIMENTAL: Account-based attribute to override the throttle by. You can set to one of the following: \"free\", \"trial\", \"paid\". Therefore, the throttle scope would be automatically set to \"account\" and ONLY the accounts based on the specified filter will have their requests throttled based on the throttle overrides while the rest are throttled based on the original configuration.","`overrides` | no | `array`[[/ThrottleOverrideObjectSchema](#throttleoverrideobjectschema)] | EXPERIMENTAL: Overrides the original throttle configuration based on a Zapier account attribute.","","#### Examples","","* `{ window: 60, limit: 100 }`","* `{ window: 600, limit: 100, scope: [ 'account', 'user' ] }`","* `{ window: 3600, limit: 10, scope: [ 'auth' ] }`","* `{ window: 3600, limit: 10, key: 'random_key', scope: [] }`","* ```","  {","    window: 3600,","    limit: 10,","    key: 'random_key-{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}',","    scope: [ 'action', 'auth' ],","    retry: false","  }","  ```","* ```","  {","    window: 3600,","    limit: 10,","    scope: [ 'auth' ],","    retry: false,","    overrides: [ { window: 3600, limit: 2, filter: 'free', retry: false } ]","  }","  ```","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{ window: 60, limit: 100, scope: [ 'zap' ] }` - _Invalid scope provided: `zap`._","* `{ limit: 10 }` - _Missing required key: `window`._","* `{ window: 600 }` - _Missing required key: `limit`._","* `{ window: 600, limit: 100, overrides: [] }` - _The overrides needs at least one item._","* `{}` - _Missing required keys: `window` and `limit`._","","-----","","## /ThrottleOverrideObjectSchema","","EXPERIMENTAL: Overrides the original throttle configuration based on a Zapier account attribute.","","#### Details","","* **Type** - `object`","* [**Source Code**](https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/zapier-platform-schema@18.5.0/packages/schema/lib/schemas/ThrottleOverrideObjectSchema.js)","","#### Properties","","Key | Required | Type | Description","--- | -------- | ---- | -----------","`window` | **yes** | `integer` | The timeframe, in seconds, within which the system tracks the number of invocations for an action. The number of invocations begins at zero at the start of each window.","`limit` | **yes** | `integer` | The maximum number of invocations for an action, allowed within the timeframe window.","`filter` | **yes** | `string` in (`'free'`, `'trial'`, `'paid'`) | Account-based attribute to override the throttle by. You can set to one of the following: \"free\", \"trial\", \"paid\". Therefore, the throttle scope would be automatically set to \"account\" and ONLY the accounts based on the specified filter will have their requests throttled based on the throttle overrides while the rest are throttled based on the original configuration.","`retry` | no | `boolean` | The effect of throttling on the tasks of the action. `true` means throttled tasks are automatically retried after some delay, while `false` means tasks are held without retry. It defaults to `true`. NOTE that it has no effect on polling triggers and should not be set.","","#### Examples","","* `{ window: 60, limit: 100, filter: 'free' }`","* `{ window: 60, limit: 100, filter: 'paid', retry: false }`","* `{ window: 60, limit: 100, filter: 'trial', retry: true }`","","#### Anti-Examples","","* `{ limit: 10 }` - <td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>By default, Zapier patches the core <code>http</code> module so that all requests (including those from 3rd-party SDKs) can be logged. Set this to true if you're seeing issues using an SDK (such as AWS).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>skipThrowForStatus</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Starting in <code>core</code> version <code>10.0.0</code>, <code>response.throwForStatus()</code> was called by default. We introduced a per-request way to opt-out of this behavior. This flag takes that a step further and controls that behavior integration-wide <strong>for requests made using <code>z.request()</code></strong>. Unless they specify otherwise (per-request, or via middleware), <a href="https://github.com/zapier/zapier-platform/blob/main/packages/cli/README.md#shorthand-http-requests">Shorthand requests</a> <em>always</em> call <code>throwForStatus()</code>. <code>z.request()</code> calls can also ignore this flag if they set <code>skipThrowForStatus</code> directly. It is important to note that for oauth2 or session auths with <code>authRefresh:true</code>, <code>401</code> status codes will throw a <code>RefreshAuthError</code> regardless of <code>skipThrowForStatus</code>, and will need to be handled manually if intervention is required.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>throwForThrottlingEarly</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Starting in <code>core</code> version <code>18.0.0</code>, 429 (throttling) responses throw a <code>ThrottledError</code> before <code>afterResponse</code> middleware runs by default. Set this flag to <code>true</code> to preserve the old behavior where <code>afterResponse</code> middleware can see and handle 429 responses. This flag can be overridden per-request by setting <code>throwForThrottlingEarly</code> directly on the request options.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cleanInputData</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>If true, Zapier removes empty strings, <code>null</code>, <code>undefined</code>, and empty Arrays or objects from <code>bundle.inputData</code> recursively before passing it to your <code>perform*</code> function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. This is a global flag that affects all the triggers and actions in your integration. The <code>cleanInputData</code> flag in <code>operation</code> takes precedence over this one.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<td>A default value that is saved the first time a Zap is created.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>list</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Acts differently when used in inputFields vs. when used in outputFields. In inputFields: Can a user provide multiples of this field? In outputFields: Does this field return an array of items of type <code>type</code>?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>children</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>array</code>[<a href="#authfieldschema">/AuthFieldSchema</a>]</td>
<td>An array of child fields that define the structure of a sub-object for this field. Usually used for line items.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>dict</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Is this field a key/value input?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>helpText</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>A human readable description of this value (IE: "The first part of a full name."). You can use Markdown.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>placeholder</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>An example value that is not saved.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>choices</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#fieldchoicesschema">/FieldChoicesSchema</a></td>
<td>An object of machine keys and human values to populate a static dropdown.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>computed</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Is this field automatically populated (and hidden from the user)? Note: Only OAuth and Session Auth support fields with this key.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFormat</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>Useful when you expect the input to be part of a longer string. Put "{{input}}" in place of the user's input (IE: "https://{{input}}.yourdomain.com").</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>isNoSecret</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Indicates if this authentication field is safe to e.g. be stored without encryption or displayed (not a secret).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Required</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>resource</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#keyschema">/KeySchema</a></td>
<td>Optionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>perform</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong></td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>How will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like <code>(z) =&gt; [{id: 123}]</code> or a request like <code>{url: 'http...'}</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performResume</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a></td>
<td>A function that parses data from a perform (which uses z.generateCallbackUrl()) and callback request to resume this action.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performGet</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>How will Zapier get a single record? If you find yourself reaching for this - consider resources and their built-in get methods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldsschema">/InputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What should the form a user sees and configures look like?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFieldGroups</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldgroupsschema">/InputFieldGroupsSchema</a></td>
<td>Defines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>outputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#outputfieldsschema">/OutputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sample</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td><code>object</code></td>
<td>What does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if <code>display.hidden</code> is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>lock</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#lockobjectschema">/LockObjectSchema</a></td>
<td>Zapier uses this configuration to ensure this action is performed one at a time per scope (avoid concurrency).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>throttle</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#throttleobjectschema">/ThrottleObjectSchema</a></td>
<td>Zapier uses this configuration to apply throttling when the limit for the window is exceeded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cleanInputData</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>If true, Zapier removes empty strings, <code>null</code>, <code>undefined</code>, and empty Arrays or objects from <code>bundle.inputData</code> recursively before passing it to your <code>perform*</code> function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. There is also a global flag with the same name in <code>App.flags</code>. This one takes precedence over the global one.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Required</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>type</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td><code>string</code> in (<code>'hook'</code>)</td>
<td>Must be explicitly set to <code>"hook"</code> unless this hook is defined as part of a resource, in which case it's optional.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>resource</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#keyschema">/KeySchema</a></td>
<td>Optionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>perform</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong></td>
<td><a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a></td>
<td>A function that processes the inbound webhook request.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performList</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>Fetch a list of items on demand during testing instead of waiting for a hook. You can also consider resources and their built-in hook/list methods. Note: this is required for public apps to ensure the best UX for the end-user. For private apps, this is strongly recommended for testing REST Hooks. Otherwise, you can ignore warnings about this property with the <code>--without-style</code> flag during <code>zapier push</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>canPaginate</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Does this endpoint support pagination via temporary cursor storage?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performSubscribe</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>Takes a URL and any necessary data from the user and subscribes. Note: this is required for public apps to ensure the best UX for the end-user. For private apps, this is strongly recommended for testing REST Hooks. Otherwise, you can ignore warnings about this property with the <code>--without-style</code> flag during <code>zapier push</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performUnsubscribe</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>Takes a URL and data from a previous subscribe call and unsubscribes. Note: this is required for public apps to ensure the best UX for the end-user. For private apps, this is strongly recommended for testing REST Hooks. Otherwise, you can ignore warnings about this property with the <code>--without-style</code> flag during <code>zapier push</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldsschema">/InputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What should the form a user sees and configures look like?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFieldGroups</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldgroupsschema">/InputFieldGroupsSchema</a></td>
<td>Defines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>outputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#outputfieldsschema">/OutputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sample</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td><code>object</code></td>
<td>What does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if <code>display.hidden</code> is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cleanInputData</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>If true, Zapier removes empty strings, <code>null</code>, <code>undefined</code>, and empty Arrays or objects from <code>bundle.inputData</code> recursively before passing it to your <code>perform*</code> function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. There is also a global flag with the same name in <code>App.flags</code>. This one takes precedence over the global one.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<markdown-accessiblity-table><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>Key</th>
<th>Required</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>resource</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#keyschema">/KeySchema</a></td>
<td>Optionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>perform</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong></td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>How will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like <code>(z) =&gt; [{id: 123}]</code> or a request like <code>{url: 'http...'}</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldsschema">/InputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What should the form a user sees and configures look like?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFieldGroups</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldgroupsschema">/InputFieldGroupsSchema</a></td>
<td>Defines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>outputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#outputfieldsschema">/OutputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sample</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td><code>object</code></td>
<td>What does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if <code>display.hidden</code> is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>lock</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#lockobjectschema">/LockObjectSchema</a></td>
<td>Zapier uses this configuration to ensure this action is performed one at a time per scope (avoid concurrency).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>throttle</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#throttleobjectschema">/ThrottleObjectSchema</a></td>
<td>Zapier uses this configuration to apply throttling when the limit for the window is exceeded.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cleanInputData</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>If true, Zapier removes empty strings, <code>null</code>, <code>undefined</code>, and empty Arrays or objects from <code>bundle.inputData</code> recursively before passing it to your <code>perform*</code> function. If you want to handle empty values yourself in your code, explicitly set this to false. There is also a global flag with the same name in <code>App.flags</code>. This one takes precedence over the global one.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<td><a href="#keyschema">/KeySchema</a></td>
<td>Optionally reference and extends a resource. Allows Zapier to automatically tie together samples, lists and hooks, greatly improving the UX. EG: if you had another trigger reusing a resource but filtering the results.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>perform</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong></td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>How will Zapier get the data? This can be a function like <code>(z) =&gt; [{id: 123}]</code> or a request like <code>{url: 'http...'}</code>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performResume</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a></td>
<td>A function that parses data from a perform (which uses z.generateCallbackUrl()) and callback request to resume this action.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>performGet</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td>oneOf(<a href="#requestschema">/RequestSchema</a>, <a href="#functionschema">/FunctionSchema</a>)</td>
<td>How will Zapier get a single record? If you find yourself reaching for this - consider resources and their built-in get methods.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>canPaginate</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>Does this search support pagination?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldsschema">/InputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What should the form a user sees and configures look like?</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>inputFieldGroups</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#inputfieldgroupsschema">/InputFieldGroupsSchema</a></td>
<td>Defines groups for organizing input fields in the UI. Each group can have a key, label, and emphasis styling.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>outputFields</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#outputfieldsschema">/OutputFieldsSchema</a></td>
<td>What fields of data will this return? Will use resource outputFields if missing, will also use sample if available.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>sample</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong> (with exceptions, see description)</td>
<td><code>object</code></td>
<td>What does a sample of data look like? Will use resource sample if missing. Requirement waived if <code>display.hidden</code> is true or if this belongs to a resource that has a top-level sample</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>lock</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#lockobjectschema">/LockObjectSchema</a></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>throttle</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><a href="#throttleobjectschema">/ThrottleObjectSchema</a></td>

</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>cleanInputData</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>boolean</code></td>
<td>If true, Zapier removes empty strings, <code>null</code>, <code>undefined</code>, and empty Arrays or objects from <code>bundle.inputData</code> recursively before passing it to your <code>perform*</code> function. This one takes precedence over the global one.</td>
</tr>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">/FieldChoiceWithLabelSchema</h2><a id="user-content-fieldchoicewithlabelschema" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: /FieldChoiceWithLabelSchema" href="#fieldchoicewithlabelschema"><svg class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">An object describing a labeled choice in a static dropdown. Useful if the value a user picks isn't exactly what the zap uses. For instance, when they click on a nickname, but the zap uses the user's full name (<a href="https://cdn.zapier.com/storage/photos/8ed01ac5df3a511ce93ed2dc43c7fbbc.png" rel="nofollow">image</a>).</p>

</tr>

</tr>
<tr>
<td>No</td>
<td>Yes</td>
<td>Array of Strings</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Yes</td>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>

<th>Key</th>
<th>Required</th>
<th>Type</th>
<th>Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>key</code></td>
<td><strong>yes</strong></td>
<td><code>string</code></td>
<td>The key to use for locking. This should be unique to the operation. While actions of different integrations with the same key and scope will never lock each other out, actions of the same integration with the same key and scope will do. User data provided for the input fields can be used in the key with the use of the curly braces referencing. For example, to access the user data provided for the input field "test_field", use <code>{{bundle.inputData.test_field}}</code>. Note that a required input field should be referenced to get user data always.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>scope</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>array</code>[<code>string</code> in (<code>'user'</code>, <code>'auth'</code>, <code>'account'</code>)]</td>
<td>By default, locks are scoped to the app. That is, all users of the app will share the same locks. If you want to restrict serial access to a specific user, auth, or account, you can set the scope to one or more of the following: 'user' - Locks based on user ids.  'auth' - Locks based on unique auth ids. 'account' - Locks for all users under a single account. You may also combine scopes. Note that "app" is included, always, in the scope provided. For example, a scope of ['account', 'auth'] would result to ['app', 'account', 'auth'].</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>timeout</code></td>
<td>no</td>
<td><code>integer</code></td>
<td>The number of seconds to hold the lock before releasing it to become accessible to other task invokes that need it. If not provided, the default set by the app will be used. It cannot be more than 180.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>
